project_name: Giga Energy Madison Digital Currency Mining Facility
aliases: Giga Energy digital currency mining facility
status_detail: City of Madison materials described a proposed 10 MW digital-currency mining/cloud-storage facility on city property north of Highway 34 and west of the southeast substation; the Planning Commission had approved a CUP and variance, but on 2026-06-16 local news reported the city would not move forward after Giga's strategic direction no longer aligned with the city's interruptible-service requirement.
notes: County official search did not surface a Lake County filing; project evidence is from City of Madison official PDFs and local news. Facility was not AI hyperscale; it was framed as digital currency mining with possible cloud storage and no operational water use.

project_name: Simple Mining Madison Digital Currency Mining Facility
aliases: Simple Mining Madison crypto mining facility
status_detail: City of Madison agenda/recap and local reporting indicate an introductory July 2026 discussion with Simple Mining for a proposed 10 MW digital-currency mining facility; talks had just begun and no vote or formal action was expected at the introductory meeting.
notes: Potential successor/alternative to Giga after Giga talks ended; developer described as Cedar Falls, Iowa-based Simple Mining. Source page from city news was visible in search snippets but returned 404 when opened; CivicClerk listing also confirms the agenda item.

status_detail: Leola Data Center applied for CUP 26-CUP-04 to construct a Data Processing Center in Spring Township; official notice set the McPherson County Zoning Board of Adjustment hearing for 2026-08-11. Prior PUC/CUP materials describe a 50 MW facility on a 20-acre leased site adjacent to MDU's Leola Substation, with initial load greater than 10 MW ramping to 50 MW.
notes: Applicant/owner listed as Leola Data Center, LLC, Attention Bill Connors. Site: 11641 358th Avenue, about 5 miles southwest of Leola; preliminary design included four 12 x 340 ft buildings, 12,288 servers, immersion cooling, and air-cooled fans. A 2024 moratorium/setback discussion delayed the earlier CUP while county rules were developed.
